_comment: Follow-up study protocol (shift-aware sample-size forecasting). Written 2026-10-12 BEFORE any of these experiments was run. These are new follow-up hypotheses, not part of the pre-specified H1-H6 of 2026-10-06. Changes only as dated amendments.
learners_note: MLP omitted for computing cost (0.83 of 2.24 CPU-hours in the original main cells); the five learners cover linear, instance-based and tree-ensemble classes.

scenarios.id: random split of each of the 24 tasks; pilot on a held-out source validation set, target = independent test set
scenarios.temporal: UNSW-NB15 S1->S2 (8 tasks) and CICIDS2017 first 60% -> last 40% of the day (6 tasks); same split as the original chrono analysis
scenarios.lovo: leave-one-variant-out within a family (CICIDS2017, NSL-KDD, CIC-IoT2023 sub-labels); target variant >= lovo_min_target unique flows, source >= lovo_min_source
scenarios.benign: attack split at random; source benign from one period (UNSW S1; CICIDS Monday), target benign from another (UNSW S2; the attack's day)

outcome.target_nstar: smallest n with mean target balanced error <= eps (log-linear interpolation); right-censored if not reached at the largest size
outcome.forecast: saturating power law (M2) fitted to the mean SOURCE-VALIDATION curve at n <= pilot_max_n, inverted at eps
categories: measurable: forecast and target n* both within the target size range
both_beyond: forecast beyond the range (or never) and target censored
false_assurance: forecast within range but target censored at a size >= 2 x forecast, or target n* > 2 x forecast
conservative_miss: forecast beyond range but target reached
outcome.unsafe: target n* > 2 x forecast, verifiable only when 2 x forecast <= largest target size (otherwise 'unverifiable')

followup_hypotheses.F1: Pilot forecasts that are accurate in distribution lose accuracy under temporal and variant shift (share within a factor of 2 lower for temporal and LOVO than for ID).
followup_hypotheses.F2: Under shift, forecast failures are predominantly unsafe under-estimates (false assurance) rather than over-estimates.
followup_hypotheses.F3: Label-free shift scores computed from the pilot and unlabelled target traffic rank unsafe forecasts above safe ones (AUROC > 0.5), and abstaining on high scores lowers the unsafe rate relative to no abstention at equal coverage to random abstention.
followup_hypotheses.F4: An abstention threshold chosen on three benchmarks transfers to the fourth (leave-one-dataset-out).
followup_hypotheses.F5: Under a pure change of attack prevalence, the label-shift-adjusted classifier two-sample test keeps its score near chance while the unadjusted test does not.
followup_hypotheses.F6: Exploratory: residual errors above 1% in four CIC-IoT2023 families persist with twice the data and with larger, internally tuned models, and are concentrated in specific sub-types.

statistics: unit of analysis = forecast (scenario x learner); uncertainty by cluster bootstrap over dataset x family (2,000 resamples), sensitivity by dataset-level bootstrap; censored n* summarised with Kaplan-Meier; all F-tests reported with exact P values and labelled follow-up/exploratory.
_amendments: 2026-10-12 (after audit A6, before any follow-up result was inspected; only 3 of 99 cells had finished and none was opened): in CIC-IoT2023 the features IAT, Number and Weight take near-constant, capture-specific values for the DDoS, DoS and Mirai families (e.g. Number = 9.5, Weight = 141.55, IAT about 8.3e7) and each alone separates these families from benign traffic with balanced error <= 0.0003 (06_Experiments/audit/A6_single_feature.csv). They are treated as collection artefacts. PRIMARY follow-up analysis for CIC-IoT2023 scenarios: these three features removed (scenario ids ending '__noart'); the runs with all features are kept as a sensitivity analysis. Other datasets unchanged.
